title: Back Propagation
body:
[[Gradient Descent]] via [[Multivariable Chain Rule]]

[[Loss Function]]
1. init [[Weight]]s
2. [[Forward Pass]]
3. calculate [[Loss Function]] wrt each [[Weight]]  

---

**Backpropagation is the [[Chain Rule]] and nothing else.** A network is a composition of layers,
so $\partial L/\partial w$ for a weight deep inside is a product of local
[[Derivative|derivatives]] along the path from that weight to the loss. It runs backward because
that order reuses the factors already computed instead of recomputing them per weight.
[[CALCULUS 1]] owns the single-variable rule; [[Multivariable Chain Rule]] in
[[MATHEMATICAL METHODS]] adds the sum over paths.
